correction.text: the city of Uruk under its fourth dynasty ('Ur-nigin: r. c. 2154 – c. 2147 BC'), in the Gutian period

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe; Cliopatria has no Uruk polity. The fourth dynasty's later kings are not on the page I read; the city is drawn alone.

correction.text: Sumer after Tirigan's defeat: Utu-hengal 'established himself as the king of Sumer' and was 'King of the four quarters of the world'; Lagash under Ur-Ningirsu II and Nam-mahani stayed outside until Ur-Nammu 'slew Nam-ha-ni' c. 2110

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Akkad and Kish are not given to Uruk: no page says Utu-hengal held them, and Kutik-Inshushinak of Elam took 'Eshnunna and Akkad, and probably Akshak' (undated on his page; Ur-Nammu reconquered them 'early in his reign').

ledger.note: 2154 BCE: Uruk's fourth dynasty under Ur-nigin. 'Ur-nigin: r. c. 2154 – c. 2147 BC'; the Gutian page: 'Early Dynastic city-states such as Lagash and Uruk began to re-assert themselves'. The year is the Akkadian Empire's end.

region.text: Sumer, 'both banks of the Tigris', Dabrum

ledger.note: 2119 BCE: Utu-hengal defeats Tirigan and is 'king of Sumer'. 'Reign: c. 2119 – c. 2112 BC', founder of the 'Fifth Dynasty of Uruk'; 'King of the four quarters of the world'; Tirigan 'fl. c. 2120 – c. 2119 BC (MC)' (Gutian page). The Ur III page: 'Around 2120 or 2055, King Utu-hegal of Uruk defeated Tirigan'.

2112 BCE: Utu-hengal dies and Ur-Nammu of Ur takes the kingship. 'In the seventh year of the kingship he died in an accident when inspecting a dam'; 'succeeded by the governor of Ur, Ur-Nammu'. The Ur III page has him dethroned by notables 'headed by Ur-Namma'; the History of Sumer page: 'Ur-Nammu of Ur defeated Utu-hegal of Uruk and founded the Third Dynasty of Ur'.

wars.name: Utu-hengal's war against Tirigan

zones.text: 'Both banks of the Tigris he had seized'; Dabrum

wars.outcome: Tirigan captured; Uruk's king 'established himself as the king of Sumer'.

certainty.note: A city and, for seven years, 'Sumer'; no line is given anywhere.

notes: A state Cliopatria lacks: the city of Uruk from the fall of Akkad (2154, Ur-nigin's fourth dynasty) to Ur-Nammu's accession (2112), including Utu-hengal's seven-year kingship of Sumer. It fills the seven-year gap between the Gutian dynasty's end (2119) and the Third Dynasty of Ur (2112) that Cliopatria leaves unlabelled. The fourth dynasty's kings after Ur-nigin and its relation to the Gutian kings (vassal or independent) are not on the pages opened: the city is drawn as its own state at confidence 2. The Early Dynastic Uruk (Gilgamesh, Lugal-kinishe-dudu, Enshakushanna, Lugal-zage-si) is inside the collective dossier sumerian-city-states; Uruk under Sin-kashid (c. 1865–1833) and its fall to Rim-Sin (c. 1801) is a separate state for the Isin-Larsa group (see larsa).
